speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I am Dr. Agent; to begin our assessment of your newborn condition, how long has the baby been ill, and what specific symptoms have you observed?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the background. Given the lack of prenatal care and immunizations, has the newborn developed any fever, lethargy, poor feeding, or signs of respiratory distress like grunting or flaring?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Syphilis.

The combination of a continuous heart murmur, bluish non-blanching macules (likely syphilitic maculopapular rash), and congenital cataracts ("cloudy lenses") strongly supports this diagnosis despite the lack of prenatal care.
